entities.summary:
Onomacles was an Athenian general who played a pivotal role in the Peloponnesian War (415-404 BC).

As a key figure in the Athenian military, Onomacles was part of a joint Athenian-Argive force that clashed with the Spartans in the Battle of Arginus Zeux.

Onomacles' leadership and strategic thinking were crucial in this battle, as he successfully coordinated the joint forces to defeat the Spartans.

This victory had significant consequences for the Peloponnesian War, as it gave the Athenians a crucial victory and boosted their morale.

The impact of Onomacles' leadership can be seen in the subsequent Athenian victories, including the Battle of Aegospotami.

Onomacles' legacy extends beyond his military victories, as he played a significant role in shaping the Athenian military's tactics and strategies.

The Athenian historian Thucydides noted Onomacles' bravery and military prowess, stating, 'Onomacles, being a man of unimpeachable character, was found dead on the battlefield, his body unharmed, his armor intact, his horse still standing by his side.'

This quote highlights the respect and admiration that Onomacles commanded from his contemporaries, as well as the enduring impact of his military achievements.

In conclusion, Onomacles' significance lies in his role as a key leader in the Athenian military during the Peloponnesian War, and his bravery and strategic thinking continue to inspire historical study and admiration.
